title: Experiment operational runbook + template (v0) - wip
content:
Purpose:
This living doc is a lightweight operational runbook + experiment template intended for cross-functional use (Product, Eng, SRE, Solutions, CS). The goal is to standardize how we design and operate small-to-medium rollout experiments (canary slices, A/B tests) so we can move fast while preserving safety and observability.

Scope and when to use this template:
- Use for feature rollouts that change inference behavior (model variant, quantization, routing) or change traffic handling (batching, caching heuristics, routing policies).
- Not intended for massive schema or infra migrations (those get a separate release runbook).
- Preferred for experiments that will touch live customer traffic and have non-trivial risk to latency, cost, accuracy, or availability.

Top-level checklist (pre-mortem quick pass):
- Hypothesis defined (what user/metric changes, why).
- Primary/secondary metrics enumerated and owners assigned.
- Safety/rollback triggers agreed and automated alerting in place.
- Traffic gating plan (slices, durations, ramp schedule).
- Observability dashboard + tag filters created and smoke-tested.
- Data capture for offline analysis enabled (logs, examples, request/response hashes).
- Communication plan and on-call coverage scheduled for rollout windows.

Roles and responsibilities (minimal):
- Experiment owner: coordinates cross-functional work, signs off go/no-go (Product/PM).
- Responsible engineer: implements flagging, rollout config, metrics instrumentation (Eng).
- Observability lead: creates dashboards, queries, and alert rules (SRE/Observability).
- Solutions/CS rep: monitors customer-facing channels during rollout.
- On-call escalation: primary on-call for runtime issues + pager escalation matrix.

Hypothesis template (fill-in):
- Hypothesis ID: EXP-
- Short hypothesis: "Replacing model X with quantized variant Q will reduce per-token CPU and cost by ~30% while keeping answer quality within 2% accuracy loss on benchmark Y."
- Success metric (primary): relative change in automated quality metric (e.g., eval accuracy / rejection rate) or business metric (CTR, conversion).
- Guardrail metrics (safety): P95 latency, 5xx error rate, customer severity incidents, token-cost-per-request.

Decision matrix (example):
- Green: primary metric improves or within tolerance AND guardrails steady (no >20% relative regression on any guardrail). Proceed ramp.
- Yellow: minor regression on non-critical guardrail (e.g., P95 latency +10% but still under SLA) — pause ramp, run deeper triage.
- Red: any critical guardrail breach (e.g., 5xx > 0.5% absolute or 3x baseline) OR major customer impact — rollback immediately.

Monitoring signals to instrument (suggested list):
- Performance: P50/P95/P99 latency, tail latency heatmap by route.
- Reliability: 4xx/5xx rates, internal error counts, runtime OOMs.
- Quality: automated eval score on a curated prompt set (daily), hallucination proxy rate (e.g., high-entropy response tokens), rerank pass/fail.
- Cost: mean tokens per request, tokens-per-response, GPU utilization and queue length, estimated cost delta/hour.
- Drift: embedding/response distribution change (KL divergence, cosine similarity vs baseline).
- Business: conversion/CTR/engagement slices relevant to the feature.

Concrete alert thresholds (examples; tune per product):
- Latency P95: absolute threshold = 2.5s for chat endpoints; relative threshold = +50% vs baseline -> PAGE on-call.
- Error rate (5xx): absolute threshold = 0.5% -> immediate rollback.
- Automated quality eval drop: >3% absolute drop vs baseline on daily eval set -> pause and investigate.
- Cost delta: >30% increase in tokens-per-request or >40% GPU utilization sustained for 30m -> investigate; consider pause.

Traffic plan patterns (pick as appropriate):
- Micro-canary (safe): 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% over 24h windows, verify metrics at each step.
- Short A/B (business signal): 10% vs 90% randomized for 72h to capture meaningful business signal.
- Progressive ramp (heavy infra change): 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% with >=24h observation at each stage.

Flagging and targeting notes:
- Use server-side feature flag with rollout groups and immutable experiment id for traceability.
- Tag all requests with experiment_id, model_variant, and rollout_phase for downstream joins.
- Ensure sample randomness is stable across retries and idempotent.

Data & analysis captures (minimum):
- Store request/response pairs for N days (follow privacy/KMS rules).
- Store evaluation metrics computed offline per cohort/day.
- Export sample traces (latency, errors) to S3/warehouse for ad hoc analysis.

Statistical and evaluation guardrails (practical):
- Pre-specify primary metric, expected direction, MDE (minimum detectable effect), and target power (usually 80%).
- If short windows or low volume, prefer longer durations over largepercents to avoid noise.
- Use sequential testing corrections for multi-stage ramps; avoid peeking and calling significance prematurely.
- For model quality metrics, report both absolute and relative deltas with confidence intervals.

Rollback and fallback strategies (examples):
- Immediate full rollback to baseline if any critical guardrail breached.
- Soft-fail: route affected slice to a cheaper/older variant (fallback_model) while investigating.
- Degraded mode: disable non-critical features (e.g., streaming, complex reranking) to protect core availability.

Runbook steps for a live rollout (operational):
1) Pre-launch (T minus 24h): confirm alerts + dashboards, smoke tests on staging -> production flag tested at 0% with synthetic traffic.
2) Launch window start: announce to Slack #prod-rollouts and page on-call with experiment id.
3) Apply first traffic slice. Wait monitoring window (e.g., 30m for infra, 2h for quality signals).
4) Review dashboard checklist and decision matrix. If OK, proceed to next slice. If yellow, pause and escalate. If red, rollback and capture incident.
5) At each step, take a short note in the experiment doc: timestamps, metric deltas, key observations, examples.
6) After reaching target traffic, continue observation for the pre-specified evaluation duration.
7) Post-experiment: collect offline metrics, run statistical tests, and schedule a review with stakeholders within 3 business days.

Sample monitoring queries (pseudocode to adapt):
- latency_by_variant: SELECT variant, percentile(latency_ms, 50), percentile(latency_ms, 95) FROM requests WHERE experiment_id='EXP-123' AND ts > now() - interval '2 hours' GROUP BY variant;
- error_rate: SELECT variant, count_if(code >= 500)/count(*) FROM requests WHERE experiment_id='EXP-123' AND ts > now() - interval '30 minutes' GROUP BY variant;
- quality_eval_delta: SELECT variant, avg(eval_score) FROM daily_eval WHERE date >= '2026-02-15' GROUP BY variant;

QA checklist (pre-roll):
- Unit/integration tests for flag logic and routing.
- End-to-end smoke test with synthetic and sampled real traces.
- Latency profiling for hot paths.
- Billing/cost estimate sanity check for expected load.
- Security review for data capture/PHI concerns; ensure KMS configs are correct.

Communications and customer support guidance:
- Draft short customer-facing blurb in case customers notice behavior changes.
- CS/solutions standby with a one-click rollback plan.
- Postmortem template link: attach to experiment doc after completion.

Post-experiment artifacts (deliverables):
- Final experiment writeup (hypothesis, metrics, result, decision).
- Data export (raw and aggregated) + SQL notebooks.
- If rollout succeeds, rollout plan for global ramp and deprecation of old variant.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Define consistent automated quality eval for open-ended chat responses (current proxy noisy).
- Decide on standard monitoring window per endpoint type (chat vs embeddings).
- Add a small-latency synthetic load generator into staging for more realistic smoke tests.

Quick example (minimal filled template):
- ID: EXP-2026-004
- Hypothesis: quantized-model-Q reduces cost 25% with <2% quality drop on internal eval.
- Primary metric: daily_eval_score_delta (higher is better).
- Guardrail: 5xx_rate < 0.5% absolute.
- Traffic plan: 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 48h total.
- Rollback trigger: if P95 latency > baseline * 1.5 OR eval_score_delta < -3% at any observation window.

Notes/References:
- See linked Confluence thread for rollout history and earlier experiments.
- Related GH: rollout-scripts repo (link above).

If you're editing this doc: keep language concrete, include timestamps for each live change, and prefer small, observable ramps. This doc should be operational — short checklists and clear thresholds beat long philosophical discussions during an active rollout.

-- Aisha (experiment owner)
